title: Joint Auction in the Online Advertising Market

problem.claim: Online advertising must serve both store owners seeking improved store positions and brand suppliers seeking to boost product sales.

gap.claim: The current advertising mode cannot satisfy the demands of both stores and brand suppliers simultaneously, and conventional auction mechanisms are unsuitable for the joint scenario.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes a joint advertising model called Joint Auction in which brand suppliers and stores collaboratively bid for advertising slots.
The paper proposes JRegNet, a neural network architecture for designing joint auctions.
The proposed design targets optimal revenue together with near-dominant-strategy incentive compatibility and individual rationality.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on synthetic and real data are reported to show that Joint Auction significantly improves platform revenue compared with known baselines.

narrative_sequence.summary: Online advertising is an important income source for e-commerce platforms, serving store owners and brand suppliers with different advertising goals.
Existing advertising and auction approaches do not simultaneously satisfy both participant groups or fit the joint scenario.
The paper introduces Joint Auction and uses JRegNet to design mechanisms targeting revenue and incentive properties.
Synthetic- and real-data experiments are reported as outperforming known baselines in platform revenue.

source_observation.claim: A joint bidding model is proposed to coordinate advertising demand from stores and brand suppliers.

interpretation.claim: Combining complementary participant objectives in one mechanism may address limitations of a single-buyer advertising model.

application.claim: Consider joint auction or mechanism designs when multiple participant types benefit from the same scarce advertising resource.

exception.claim: Conventional auction mechanisms may not transfer directly to settings with collaborative bidding by multiple participant types.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the auction rules, bidding protocol, or allocation and payment mechanisms.
The abstract does not provide experiment settings, datasets, baseline identities, revenue values, or statistical details.
The abstract does not quantify the incentive-compatibility, individual-rationality, or near-optimality guarantees.
